ns0:summary.p: Returns a dateTime value for a Unix time.

ns0:rules.p: The function returns a dateTime value in UTC timezone for the Unix time specified by $value in milliseconds. The Unix time is defined in .

If the implementation supports data types from XSD 1.1 then the returned value will be an instance of xs:dateTimeStamp. Otherwise, the only guarantees are that it will be an instance of xs:dateTime and will have a timezone component.

ns0:notes.p: By calling this convenience function, it can be ensured that the correct timezone is used for computing the Unix time.
Note that Unix time does not account for leap seconds. It assumes that every day has 86,400 seconds.
A negative value denotes an instant before 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.

ns0:example.p: Calculate the Unix time associated with a xs:dateTime value:
ns0:example.eg: let $value := current-dateTime() return ($value - unix-dateTime()) div seconds(0.001)

ns0:change.p: Changed the type of $value to xs:integer?, allowing instants before 1970.
